name: Roll20
summary: A long-running browser VTT with sheets for a very wide range of systems; suits groups who want to play online with nothing to install.

price.note: Plus about $5.99/mo, Pro about $10.99/mo, Elite (Oct 2025) $12.50-14.99/mo; sources disagree. Players free

accounts.note: Players join with a free Roll20 account

fog.note: Fog of war and Explorer mode

lighting.note: Dynamic Lighting built in; listed as a Plus/Pro (GM) feature

mapbuild.note: Drawing tools; Roll20 also owns Dungeon Scrawl, a separate map maker (Pro on Elite)

sheets.note: Character sheets for many systems, compendium, Demiplane sheet integration

dice.note: 3D dice, off by default, turned on in settings

phone.note: Mobile app delisted Feb 2026; mobile browser for character sheets

offline.note: Hosted service; no self-host option found

opensource.note: Core closed; community character sheet code is public on GitHub

modding.note: Mod Scripts (API) on Pro and above; custom sheets

community.note: Calls itself 'the #1 tabletop for playing RPGs online'; one of the largest VTT user bases

upsides: Nothing to install; runs in a browser
Sheets and official content for a very wide range of game systems
Free tier is enough to run a game; players never pay
downsides: Dynamic lighting and Mod scripts need a paid GM subscription
Hosted only; no way to run your own server
Official mobile app was delisted in 2026

sources.label: Help center: subscriptions (not readable from here)

name: Foundry VTT
summary: A one-time-purchase VTT you host yourself, with deep rules automation and a huge module ecosystem; suits GMs who like to tinker.

dims.note: Core is 2D; true 3D comes from the third-party 3D Canvas module (TheRipper93)

platform.note: GM runs the app or a server; players join in a browser

price.note: $50 licence for the GM; players pay nothing

accounts.note: Only the licence holder needs a foundryvtt.com account; players join by link

fog.note: Fog of war with exploration memory

lighting.note: Walls, lights and vision modes in core

mapbuild.note: Walls, tiles and drawings over imported maps; builders via modules (3D Canvas premium)

levels.note: v14 Scene Levels: stacked floors in one scene, stairs, per-level walls and lights

sheets.note: Game systems (e.g. D&D 5e, Pathfinder 2e) with rules automation; WotC and Paizo partners

ddb.note: Beyond20 supports Foundry; community DDB-Importer module also exists

dice.note: Core dice roller; 3D dice via the Dice So Nice module

phone.note: FAQ: mobile not supported in core; some modules add Android support

offline.note: Self-hosted on the GM's computer or a server; internet needed to activate licence

opensource.note: Closed core; many systems and modules are open source

ai.note: No built-in AI feature found; AI content policy bars AI-made prepared content

modding.note: Module and system API; packages reviewed before listing

community.note: Large package ecosystem; 3D Canvas alone was updated within the last two weeks

upsides: Pay once, no subscription; players never pay
Deep rules automation for many systems and a vast module library
Self-host or run offline on your own machine
downsides: Steep learning curve; modules can break between versions
GM must host it or pay for hosting
No phone support in core

name: Fantasy Grounds (Unity)
summary: A desktop VTT with heavy rules automation and many officially licensed games, free to play since November 2025; suits rules-heavy groups.

platform.note: Desktop installers and Steam; browser Online Reader is for reading modules only

price.note: Free to play since 2025-11-08: no licence or subscription; rulesets and modules sold separately

accounts.note: Free Fantasy Grounds account to log in

lighting.note: Dynamic lighting, vision and line of sight

mapbuild.note: Press kit: build maps, add lighting and walls; extent of drawing tools unclear

sheets.note: Native automation of combat, effects, conditions, saves

ddb.note: No official integration found; community import extensions reported

offline.note: GM's computer hosts; cloud hosting also offered

opensource.note: Closed core; rulesets are readable Lua

modding.note: Extensions, rulesets and modules; FG Forge marketplace

community.note: Went free to play at FG Con Online in Nov 2025; long-running forums

upsides: Free to play with no licence or subscription
Strong rules automation for many officially licensed games
Runs on Windows, Mac and Linux
downsides: Desktop install needed for every player; no phone play
Official content for most games is sold separately
Interface takes time to learn

name: Owlbear Rodeo
summary: A minimal, fast browser VTT where players join by link without an account, extended through an extension store; suits GMs who want simplicity.

alive.how: official site answered 200 (browser user agent; plain requests get 403)

dims.note: Infinite 2D canvas; square, hex and isometric grids

platform.note: Players open the room link in a web browser

price.note: Nestling free; Fledgling and Bestling paid (more storage, rooms, Forecast); prices shown in-app

accounts.note: Players can join anonymously; GM needs an account

fog.note: Manual fog tools built in; Forecast auto-detects rooms (paid tiers)

lighting.note: Walls, doors and lights through the official Dynamic Fog extension

mapbuild.note: Drawing tools for sketching maps on the fly

sheets.note: No rules in core; sheets and initiative come from extensions

ddb.note: Beyond20 does not list Owlbear; community extensions may exist

dice.note: Official dice extension with 3D physics dice

offline.note: Hosted service; no self-host option found

opensource.note: Maker says much of it is open source (e.g. dice roller, music app); core closed

ai.note: Forecast uses a computer-vision pipeline for fog; no generative AI found

stage.note: Version 2.4 (May 2026); Forecast out of beta Oct 2026

community.note: Small team shipping steadily (2.4 May 2026, Forecast Oct 2026); active Discord and subreddit

upsides: Players join by link with no account
Clean, fast and easy to learn
Official extensions add dynamic fog and 3D dice
downsides: No rules or sheets in core; extensions needed
Dynamic lighting is an extension, not core
Auto fog detection (Forecast) is paid-tier only

sources.label: Blog: On Plagiarism, AI and Centaurs

name: TaleSpire
summary: A 3D tabletop where you build scenes from tiles and props and throw physical dice; suits groups who want a lush 3D table and buy one copy each.

dims.note: Full 3D scene built from tiles and props

platform.note: Windows and macOS (Apple Silicon only); Linux via Proton being worked on

price.note: $24.99; non-owners join via free Guest Edition on a Seat the owner buys (one-time)

accounts.note: Steam account for owners and guests

fog.note: Real fog of war not shipped; GMs hide areas manually with hide volumes

lighting.note: Line of sight hides minis; no light-and-wall vision

mapbuild.note: Tile, prop and slab building is the core of the product

levels.note: True 3D; flying, elevation and a cut plane for floors

sheets.note: Rules-agnostic core; sheets via Symbiotes mods

ddb.note: No official integration; FAQ calls a partnership unlikely

dice.note: Physical dice you throw onto the board

offline.note: Central servers only; peer-to-peer is planned

modding.note: Symbiotes (web-view API), TaleWeaverLite models, mod.io browser

community.note: Steam: Very Positive, 90% of 3,316 reviews; recent 76% of 17

upsides: Beautiful 3D scenes that are fast to build from tiles
Physical 3D dice everyone sees land
One-time price, all official content free
downsides: No real fog of war after years in Early Access
Every player needs a copy or a GM-bought Seat
Always online; no offline or LAN play

name: Alchemy RPG
summary: A cinematic VTT built around music, animated scenes and story, with tactical maps available; suits story-first groups.

dims.note: Animated scene art plus a tactical map layer with grids

platform.note: Web plus Windows, Mac and Linux downloads

price.note: Free Unlimited $0; Alchemist supporter tier $8/mo adds perks, not features

fog.note: GM brushes fog on and off by hand

sheets.note: Access to every game system plus a homebrew system builder

ai.note: Site has a 'stance on generative AI' FAQ; answer not readable

modding.note: Homebrew System Builder; no API found

community.note: Homepage carries testimonials from Avantris and Rowdy Crypt; active Discord

upsides: Everything is free; the paid tier only adds supporter perks
Music, ambience and animated scenes for story-driven play
Runs in a browser or as a desktop app
downsides: Tactical tools are lighter than map-first VTTs
Dynamic lighting not documented
Fog of war is manual brushing only

name: Demiplane
summary: A character builder, digital rulebook and campaign companion for many non-D&D systems; not a map table. Suits players who want official sheets.

dims.note: No map table of its own; tabletop play happens on Roll20

price.note: Free sign-up; rulebooks and content sold per game

accounts.note: Sign-up to save characters and join campaigns

fog.note: No map table of its own; tabletop play happens on Roll20

lighting.note: No map table of its own; tabletop play happens on Roll20

mapbuild.note: No map table of its own; tabletop play happens on Roll20

levels.note: No map table of its own; tabletop play happens on Roll20

sheets.note: Official character builders and sheets per system (Nexus pages)

modding.note: Homebrew (beta) in the app menu; no API found

community.note: Its sheets are being brought into Roll20 (public beta reported)

upsides: Official sheets and rules for many non-D&D games
Fast rules lookup in digital books
Works with Roll20 for play on a map
downsides: Not a VTT: no map, tokens or fog
Content is bought per game system
Needs Roll20 or another tool for map play

name: D&D Beyond Maps
summary: D&D Beyond's own simple browser VTT, tied to your D&D Beyond characters and books; suits D&D groups who already use D&D Beyond.

price.note: Free for all registered users since 2025-09-16; Master Tier adds map uploads and storage

accounts.note: Anyone with a D&D Beyond account can use it

fog.note: Fog of war, polygonal fog added in 2025

lighting.note: Users ask for dynamic lighting, walls and token vision in roadmap comments

mapbuild.note: Stickers and drawing on official or uploaded maps; no builder

sheets.note: Uses D&D Beyond character sheets and rules content

ddb.note: It is D&D Beyond's own tool

offline.note: Hosted service; no self-host option found

community.note: 2026 roadmap comments mostly request dynamic lighting, token vision and walls

upsides: Free, and wired straight into D&D Beyond characters and books
Official adventures come with ready maps
Very simple to start for D&D groups
downsides: D&D only
No dynamic lighting or walls yet
Still labelled beta

sources.label: Maps free for all registered users (2025-09-17)

name: Tabletop Simulator
summary: A physics sandbox for any tabletop game, with an RPG kit, Lua scripting and a huge Steam Workshop; suits groups who like building their own table.

alive.how: official site and Steam page answered 200

platform.note: Windows, macOS, SteamOS/Linux; HTC Vive and Oculus Rift

price.note: $19.99, 4-pack $59.99; for DLC only the host needs to own it

accounts.note: Steam account and own copy per player

lighting.note: Backgrounds change lighting; no vision system found

mapbuild.note: RPG Kit tilesets, furniture and figurines to build scenes

levels.note: Free 3D space; stack and stage anything

sheets.note: Tablet for character sheets; rules only via scripted mods

community.note: Steam: Overwhelmingly Positive, 96% of 32,148 reviews; recent 97% of 277

upsides: Huge Steam Workshop of community tables and assets
Lua scripting can automate almost anything
VR and non-VR players can share a table
downsides: A general game sandbox, not an RPG tool; few RPG rules
No vision or dynamic lighting system found
Every player needs their own copy

name: Shard Tabletop
summary: A D&D 5e-focused browser VTT with built-in character building and rules automation; suits 5e groups online or at the table.

price.note: Free SRD play for GMs and players; reported tiers $2.99, $5.99, $9.99/mo

accounts.note: Players build characters in their own account

fog.note: Rectangle, polygon and brush fog tools; preset fog regions on some maps

lighting.note: Line of sight from walls, lighting and darkvision on configured maps

ddb.note: D&D Beyond import disabled after it broke

dice.note: Animated dice mentioned; type not confirmed

phone.note: Site says it works on any device

modding.note: Content extensions for other settings, no programming; no API found

community.note: No community size figure checked this session

upsides: Free 5e SRD play for GMs and players
Character building and rules automation in one tool
Dynamic lighting and fog of war built in
downsides: Built around D&D 5e; other systems need extensions
D&D Beyond import was turned off
Map building tools not documented

name: Let's Role
summary: A browser VTT with sheets for hundreds of systems, a no-code system builder and a mobile app; suits groups playing less common games.

platform.note: Web plus a syncing mobile app (Android linked; iOS not confirmed)

price.note: Basic free (ads on mobile); Explorer €2/mo yearly, Traveler €5/mo, Adventurer €9/mo; players free

accounts.note: Players and GMs create an account first

sheets.note: Sheets for hundreds of systems; roll from the sheet

phone.note: Mobile app that syncs with desktop

modding.note: System Builder with JavaScript for advanced logic

community.note: Claims hundreds of supported systems; Discord community

upsides: All features free; paid tiers add storage and cosmetics
Sheets for hundreds of systems plus a system builder
Mobile app alongside the browser version
downsides: Free tier storage is 125 MB
Ads on the free mobile app
Fog of war not documented

price.note: Free forever; Pro $9.99/mo or $89.99/yr with AI credits; players' cost not stated

accounts.note: Players join by invite link or username

fog.note: Fog of war on the free tier

lighting.note: Dynamic lighting on the free tier

mapbuild.note: AI map and scene generation (Pro); manual drawing not confirmed

sheets.note: Call of Cthulhu and universal sheets; automation not described

dice.note: Rolls from sheets and a dice roller; 3D not confirmed

ai.note: GM assistant, adventure, map, token and note generation (Pro)

modding.note: Developer API and MCP server; no mod system found

community.note: No community size figure checked this session

Phone apps for iOS and Android
Developer API and MCP server for tools
